$comment: The committed MySQL dialect denylist that db.dialect-floor.guard reads (10-testing-and-quality.md, guard table; 03-data-model.md section 1.1; 11-operations-and-deployment.md 'The MySQL dialect rule', D03-23). Every statement Iridium executes must have identical semantics on MySQL 8.4.11 and 9.7.2. The floor is 8.4.11: a construct that requires 9.x is forbidden, and a construct 8.4 merely deprecates is forbidden too, because a deprecation is a removal with a date on it. Entries are data, so adding a construct is a one-line change and never a code change.
$matching: Each token is matched as a case-sensitive literal substring over apps/server/src/**/*.ts, apps/server/migrations/**/*.ts, infra/docker/mysql/**, docs/ops/*.sql and apps/server/src/ops/**. Case-sensitivity is what separates the SQL keyword VECTOR from the English word in a comment about a Yjs state vector; every lowercase token below is a literal variable, plugin or flag name.

Every role is IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password on both lines; infra/docker/mysql/init/01_roles.sh asserts it and fails container initialisation otherwise (03-data-model.md section 1.1).
An unknown variable makes mysqld exit at startup, and one my.cnf is mounted into every environment. Use authentication_policy = caching_sha2_password, the supported spelling on 8.4 and 9.x.
Every Iridium table is InnoDB; innodb_ft_min_token_size = 2 is the setting that governs the FULLTEXT tokenizer, and it is frozen into ft_note_search when migration 0020 builds it.
Use --source-data. The backup set's mysqldump invocation is one exported constant, so a removed flag would first fail in a restore drill.

The VALUES(col) function inside ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE is deprecated on both supported lines; use the row-alias form `INSERT ... VALUES (...) AS new ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE col = new.col` (03-data-model.md section 9.2, D03-23). The token is the function-call spelling with no space, so write an ordinary value list as `VALUES (...)`.
